subject: Discovery recap — BrightCart embeddings & rerank
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@brightcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap — BrightCart embeddings & rerank

Alex / Priya — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re aligned. Please flag anything I missed.

Pain points you shared:
- Search relevance has degraded as catalog grew (approx 50M SKU-level product records).
- Current reranking is expensive and brittle: you’re doing a hybrid lexical + dense workflow in-house, with nightly batch re-embeds and per-query FAISS lookups that require manual tuning.
- Latency spikes under peak traffic (holiday promotions) causing cart abandonment.

Current stack (as discussed):
- Primary store: Postgres + Redis cache for session state.
- Vector index: FAISS (self-hosted) for nearest-neighbor, thin orchestrator for sharding.
- Feature pipeline: Airflow nightly jobs to re-embed ~100k updated records/day; real-time upserts limited and rate-limited.

Success criteria you described:
- P99 rerank latency < 150ms for user query + rerank step (target 100–120ms ideally).
- Per-query embedding + index cost target <$0.01 at scale.
- End-user relevance uplift: +8–12% CTR on recommendations / search conversions.
- Operational: reduce manual tuning and make re-embedding predictable during peaks.

Workload details we captured:
- Index scale: ~50M product docs, average vector dim 768, average doc size small (title + short attrs).
- Query pattern: bursty with hourly peaks (10x baseline) and weekly batch updates; real-time upserts ~1–2k/day but expect to increase with promotions.
- Batch patterns: daily full/partial re-embed of changed docs (100k/day), larger seasonal rebuilds during catalog syncs.

Potential Redwood fit / options we discussed:
- Embeddings + rerank flow with Redwood-hosted endpoints (dedicated or private) to control latency; automatic prefix caching to reduce repeat token cost.
- Vector DB choices: integrate with your FAISS or recommend managed vectors (Pinecone/Weaviate) with sharding guidance — Redwood can route by region/latency and fall back to a cheaper model variant during overload.
- Cost optimizations: batching, KV cache for hot prefixes, and model quantization suggestions to lower per-token cost while preserving relevance.

Immediate next steps (Agreed):
1) I’ll share a short technical checklist for load/embedding characteristics + a sample dataset (anonymized) so we can estimate latency/cost. (Attachment: BrightCart-discovery-notes.pdf)
2) Alex/Priya to share an example query profile (CSV) and a small sample of product metadata for a quick perf estimate.
3) Follow-up technical session w/ Ben & Dylan (Redwood infra leads) to deep-dive on index topology and upsert patterns — target next week.

If that all looks right I’ll schedule the deep-dive and prepare a preliminary perf/cost estimate based on your sample.

Thanks,
Marissa
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0142

---
Attachments: BrightCart-discovery-notes.pdf (overview + anonymized example), BrightCart-MAP.xlsx (mutual action plan template)

From: Alex Nguyen <alex@brightcart.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@brightcart.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — BrightCart embeddings & rerank

Thanks Marissa — this is great and covers everything we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Index scale is closer to 52M records with ~5M fairly frequently updated SKUs (promotional fast-changing set).
- Real-time upserts currently spike during campaigns to ~10k/hour (we throttled historically, but want to support higher rates).
- Target cost per query is aggressive: <$0.01 end-to-end — we’re open to hybrid approaches (smaller candidate set lexical + dense rerank) if that helps hit the cost target.

I attached the sample query profile and a small product dump (anonymized) — should be in a separate secure link, but we’re happy to upload to whatever you prefer.

Can we aim to have the technical deep-dive Thursday next week? Ben and a backend engineer (Priya) will join. Also please include your recommended vector DB options and any suggested pilot size (we were thinking 5–10M sample index to start).

—Alex
Head of Search & Personalization | BrightCart
alex@brightcart.com
+1 206-555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@brightcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — BrightCart embeddings & rerank

Perfect — thanks for those details, Alex. Thursday next week works for us. I’ll get a calendar invite out shortly for a 60-minute deep-dive.

Pre-read & ask for the deep-dive:
- Please upload the sample CSV (query profile) and the anonymized product dump to the Drive link I shared in the related links. We’ll use that to run a small-scale perf estimate.
- Pilot recommendation: start with 5–10M vectors (sample of high-traffic SKUs + long-tail stratified) to evaluate latency and cost metrics; we’ll show both FAISS-based and managed-vector baselines.
- For the deep-dive, Ben and Dylan will cover indexing topology, shard sizing, and upsert throughput considerations.

Agenda for the technical session (60m):
1) Quick recap (5m)
2) Review sample data & query profile (10m)
3) Perf/cost baseline walk-through (20m)
4) Index topology & scaling strategy (15m)
5) Next steps / pilot plan & ownership (10m)

We’ll prepare a short perf/cost write-up after the call and a suggested pilot SOW (high-level). If anything changes on timing, let me know and we’ll adjust.

Thanks — looking forward to it.
Marissa

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — BrightCart embeddings & rerank

Looping in a couple of quick technical clarifications ahead of the deep-dive: 
- Can you confirm the average embedding dimension and model family you’re using today (you mentioned 768 but just want the exact config)?
- For FAISS: are you using IVF+PQ or HNSW in production today? That will change our recommendations for sharding and memory footprint.
- Do you have any SLOs for cold-start throughput (e.g., bulk upserts after a catalog sync) beyond the steady-state upsert rate?

We’ll prepare two pilot options: 1) FAISS-compatible pilot to validate on your existing stack (min changes) and 2) managed-vector pilot (Pinecone/Weaviate) with Redwood routing and fallback for peak traffic. Each pilot will include expected latency/CAD estimates for the 5–10M sample.

Thanks — Ben
